ticker.pick_prompt: Search or pick a ticker from the sidebar list.
ticker.pct_portfolio_help: This position's value today vs all your open positions
ticker.unrealised_pl_help: Latest price vs what you paid on average (FIFO, fees included). It can change until you sell.
ticker.history_failed: Couldn't load the price history for this ticker — try again in a moment.
ticker.history_empty: No price history available for this ticker — it may be delisted or very thinly traded.
ticker.span_hint_touch: Two fingers on the chart: change between two dates
ticker.span_hint_mouse: Right-click (two-finger click on a trackpad) to measure between dates
ticker.sma20_help: Price above SMA20 = short-term uptrend, below = downtrend
ticker.ai_analyze_help: Ask the assistant for a full analysis of {ticker}
ticker.ai_prompt: Analyze {name} ({ticker}): what the business does and what competitive advantages it has, how the fundamentals and recent growth look, whether today's valuation is demanding or reasonable against its own history and its peers, the main risks, and how it fits my portfolio and my investor profile. Finish with a three-line thesis and what to watch over the next few months.
ticker.ai_prompt_fund: Analyze the fund {name} ({ticker}): what it holds and how concentrated the basket is, its cost and how well it tracks its index, the exposure it really gives me, the main risks, and where it overlaps with what I already own. Finish with a three-line verdict and what to watch.
ticker.ai_prompt_crypto: Analyze {name} ({ticker}): what the asset is and what moves its price, how it has behaved lately and against the rest of the market, the main risks — volatility, regulation, custody — and what weight it can reasonably carry in a portfolio like mine. Finish with a three-line verdict and what to watch.
ticker.crypto_caption: Quoted in {quote}. Fundamentals, insider filings, earnings and DCF don't apply to crypto — those sections are hidden for this asset.
ticker.chart_annual_title: Revenue, net income & diluted EPS by year
ticker.annual_caption: Hatched bars = analyst consensus revenue; dashed = consensus EPS (right axis) with shaded low-high analyst range (yfinance); years beyond published estimates extrapolated (revenue at next-FY consensus growth, EPS at long-term growth with next-FY fallback).
ticker.fundamentals_failed: Couldn't load the fundamental KPIs for this ticker — the data source returned nothing.
ticker.kpi_peg_help: yfinance PEG unreliable — cross-check analyst consensus (Koyfin/TIKR)
ticker.moat_insufficient: Not enough statement history to score a moat — needs at least 3 of the 5 pillars (ROIC, margins, growth, FCF, dilution).
ticker.moat_caption: Quant proxies from {years} filed years — the score sees what a moat leaves in the numbers, not its cause (brand, network effects, switching costs). Screen, not verdict.
ticker.insider_caption: SEC Form 4 — officers, directors and 10% owners trading their own stock. Open-market buys (P) and sells (S) are the signal; grants, option exercises and tax withholding are shown but excluded from the buy/sell net.
ticker.insider_caption_bafin: MAR Article 19 via BaFin — officers, directors and people closely associated with them trading their own company's stock, notified within 3 business days. Buys and sells are the signal; BaFin publishes an average price and an aggregated euro volume, so the share count is derived (volume / price). German issuers only, last 12 months.
ticker.no_form4: No insider activity: this issuer has no recent Form 4 filings on record with the SEC.
ticker.no_form4_non_us: No insider activity: this symbol isn't a US listing and isn't in BaFin's German directors' dealings register either. Only SEC-registered issuers file Form 4 — if the company also trades in the US, open its US ticker.
ticker.cluster_buying: Cluster buying — multiple insiders bought on the open market over the window and net flow is positive.
ticker.selling_dominates: Selling dominates open-market insider flow over the window.
ticker.chart_insider_title: Open-market insider buys vs sells by month ({ccy})
ticker.related_help: People-also-watch peers from Yahoo Finance — tap to add to the comps table.
ticker.extra_none: No symbol matches that — try the company name.
ticker.medals_caption: 🥇🥈🥉 = best composite rank across the comparable KPIs (valuation, quality, growth, leverage — each metric ranked across the set, size ignored).
ticker.pick_peers: Pick peers to build the comps table.
ticker.kpi_sources_caption: Verification hierarchy: SEC EDGAR (primary, 10-K/10-Q) > stockanalysis.com (10y ratios) > Macrotrends (15-20y trends) > Koyfin/TIKR (multi-company comps). yfinance loads the numbers; EDGAR confirms them. All KPIs defined in {n} entries of KPI_SOURCES.
ticker.pe_insufficient: Couldn't rebuild a P/E history — no quarterly EPS filings available for this ticker (non-US filer without an FMP key, or too few quarters).
ticker.kpi_pe_current_help: Latest close divided by the trailing-12-month diluted EPS known that day, rebuilt from quarterly filings. Can differ slightly from the P/E (TTM) in the fundamentals row (different EPS vintage).
ticker.kpi_pe_avg_help: Mean of the daily trailing P/E over the selected range.
ticker.kpi_pe_premium_help: Premium (+) or discount (−) of the current P/E against its own average over the selected range.
ticker.pe_caption: Reconstructed series: split-adjusted close over the trailing-12-month diluted EPS (GAAP) rebuilt from quarterly filings ({source}), stepped forward on each filing date — each day only uses figures that were already public. Loss-making stretches (negative TTM EPS) are omitted.
ticker.pe_divergence: This reconstructed P/E ({cur}) is {diff}% away from the P/E (TTM) in Fundamentals ({fund}). Usual cause: the latest reported quarter is already in Yahoo's trailing EPS, but its 10-Q/10-K hasn't been filed with SEC EDGAR yet — this series catches up on the filing date. Adjusted vs GAAP EPS can also widen the gap.
ticker.fund_ter_help: Annual cost of holding the fund, taken out of its price every day (TER). 0.20% on 10,000 EUR is 20 EUR a year.
ticker.fund_aum_help: Total net assets the fund manages. Yahoo often leaves this blank for UCITS listings — a missing figure says nothing about the fund.
ticker.fund_yield_help: Income paid out over the last year as a share of price. An accumulating (Acc) share class reinvests instead of paying, and reports nothing here.
ticker.fund_turnover_help: Share of the portfolio traded over a year. High turnover means trading costs on top of the expense ratio.
ticker.fund_duration_help: Effective duration in years: roughly how many percent the fund moves for a 1-point move in rates, in the opposite direction.
ticker.fund_top10_help: What the ten largest disclosed holdings add up to — the concentration floor of the basket.
ticker.fund_holdings_caption: The {n} largest disclosed holdings, {pct} of the fund — Yahoo publishes the top ten only, so the rest of the basket isn't shown here.
ticker.fund_no_holdings: No holdings published for this fund.
ticker.fund_caption: A fund holds companies rather than being one, so there are no statements, insider filings, earnings dates or comparables below — cost, basket and exposure take their place. Your portfolio's sector allocation looks through this fund to what it holds.
ticker.cef_nav_help: Net asset value: what the fund's holdings are worth per share, struck once a day after the close. A closed-end fund's price can sit well away from it.
ticker.cef_premium_help: Price over NAV, minus one, on the same session. Negative is a discount: you pay less than the holdings are worth. Closed-end funds often trade at a lasting discount, and it can widen or close.
ticker.cef_distribution_help: The current annual distribution as a share of the price. Part of it can be return of capital rather than income — the fund's Section 19 notices say how much.
ticker.cef_ter_help: Total annual expenses from the fund's SEC fee table, as a share of net assets. It includes the interest paid on leverage, which is why it runs higher than an ETF's.
ticker.cef_net_assets_help: Holdings minus everything the fund owes, from its latest monthly N-PORT filing with the SEC.
ticker.cef_leverage_help: Liabilities as a share of total assets on the latest N-PORT: borrowings and preferred shares, plus payables for trades in flight — read it as a ceiling. Leverage magnifies both the income and the swings.
ticker.cef_check_ok: {metric} cross-checked: {official} in the {official_source} for {date} matches {market} from {market_source}.
ticker.cef_check_off: **{metric}: the sources disagree.** The {official_source} for {date} says {official}; {market_source} says {market} for the same session. Both are shown as published — check the fund's own site before relying on either.
ticker.cef_check_none: {metric}: the {official_source} for {date} says {official}; {market_source} has no figure for that session, so it is not cross-checked.
ticker.cef_check_absent: The fund files no NAV or premium in XBRL with the SEC, so NAV and premium come from Yahoo alone and are not cross-checked.
ticker.cef_holdings_caption: The {n} largest issuers among {count} positions in the SEC N-PORT for {date}, {pct} of net assets. Bond lines are grouped by issuer.
ticker.cef_caption: A closed-end fund has a fixed number of shares that trade on the exchange at their own price, above or below what the holdings are worth (NAV). Yahoo lists it as an ordinary share; these figures come from the fund's SEC filings and Yahoo's NAV line instead. It holds securities rather than being a company, so there are no statements, insider filings, earnings dates or comparables below.
ticker.asset_stock_line: A share of one company: its price follows what it earns and what the market expects it to earn. Read the results, valuation and margins.
ticker.asset_equity_fund_line: A basket of shares in a single line: it rises and falls with its market. Read the cost, what it holds and how concentrated it is.
ticker.asset_bond_fund_line: A basket of bonds: it pays interest and its price moves against interest rates. Read the distribution yield, the duration and the cost.
ticker.asset_money_market_line: Cash that earns close to the central bank's rate; the price climbs slowly, almost in a straight line. Read the annualised yield against the policy rate and the cost, not the chart.
ticker.asset_closed_end_line: A fund with a fixed number of shares that trades on an exchange: it can cost more or less than its holdings are worth. Read the premium or discount and the distribution.
ticker.asset_crypto_line: A cryptocurrency: no earnings and no accounts, it trades around the clock and moves far more than a stock. Read the trend, the volume and the circulating supply.
ticker.asset_index_line: Measures a market; it cannot be bought directly — you follow it with an ETF or an index fund.
ticker.cash_yield_help: What the fund earned over the last 3 months, compounded to a year. Read off its own price: an accumulating money-market fund adds each day's interest to its value. It is what it earned, not a promise: it follows the policy rate when that moves.
ticker.policy_rate_help: What the central bank pays on overnight money. A money-market fund in that currency earns close to it, less its cost; when the bank cuts, the fund earns less. Source: FRED.
ticker.cash_caption: A money-market fund is cash in the shape of a fund: no statements, no results, no comparables, and its chart is almost a straight line. What matters is what it earns against the policy rate, what it costs, and that the yield falls when the central bank cuts.
ticker.ai_prompt_cash: Analyze the money-market fund {name} ({ticker}): what it earns against its central bank's policy rate, its cost, how it gets that yield (bills, repos or a swap) and what risk it really carries, and whether it suits me better than an interest-bearing account or Treasury bills. Finish with a three-line verdict and what to watch.
ticker.ev_cycle: Cycle events (h halving · e ETF · m Merge)
ticker.ath_help: How far the price sits under the coin's all-time high. A coin 60% under its peak is the normal state of the asset, not a tail event.
ticker.coin_weight_help: This coin's value over all the crypto in your book.
ticker.sleeve_help: All your crypto over your whole book. Allocators who hold crypto at all usually keep it at 2–10%: under 2% barely moves the book, over 10% lets crypto's 70% drawdowns set the whole book's.
ticker.harvest_line: Selling it today would realise {loss} and save about {saving} in tax this year.
ticker.harvest_window: Buying it back before {date} would defer the loss instead.
ticker.harvest_blocked: Selling it today would realise {loss}, but you bought inside the repurchase window: the loss would be deferred, not deducted.
ticker.cycle_caption: Cycle context, not a forecast: these levels marked past tops and bottoms, and every cycle has broken some of them.
ticker.fear_greed_help: The Crypto Fear & Greed Index (alternative.me), 0–100, from volatility, momentum, social media and dominance. Extremes have tended to come before reversals.
ticker.btc_dominance_help: Bitcoin's share of the whole crypto market's capitalisation. Rising means money is moving into bitcoin and out of the rest.
ticker.mayer_help: Price over its 200-day average. Under 0.8 has marked past bottoms; over 2.4 marked past blow-off tops.
ticker.w200_help: Price over its 200-week average of weekly closes. Past bear markets bottomed near it.
ticker.vol30_help: Annualised standard deviation of daily returns over the past 30 days. A large stock runs at 20–30%; bitcoin usually at 40–70%.
ticker.vs_btc_help: How much {coin} beat or lagged bitcoin over 90 days, in the same currency. An altcoin that rose 20% while bitcoin rose 40% lost ground.
ticker.vs_nasdaq_help: Bitcoin against the Nasdaq 100 (QQQ) over 90 days, both in US dollars — the risk asset it trades with.
ticker.halving_help: Bitcoin's block reward halves every 210,000 blocks, about four years. The bar is the share of the way to the next one, whose date is an estimate.
ticker.funding_help: What leveraged longs pay shorts on the perpetual swap, per eight hours. The resting rate is 0.01%; well above it is leverage piling in on the long side, negative is shorts paying.
ticker.open_interest_help: The value of the perpetual swap's open positions, in US dollars. The weekly change is counted in contracts, so a price move does not read as positions opened.
ticker.positioning_caption: Read live from the first exchange that lists the coin's USDT perpetual. Crowded leverage has come before the sharpest flushes; it does not say when.
ticker.fdv_ratio_help: Fully diluted value over today's market cap. 1.0× means the whole supply is already out; well above it, supply still to unlock that the market will have to absorb.
